Mary | TV & Movie Recs 🎉 on Instagram: "Typically I would never ever purposefully spoil a movie the same weekend that it was released, but for “The Drama” it seems like a responsible thing to do ❤️.

I genuinely think The Drama was VERY well done, it was a really good movie!! The performances were fantastic and the story actually handled a really intense conversation in a very impactful and often very nuanced way. But I just wish I had known that this is the type of movie I was in for. 

Have you seen it? Will you see it? Let me know below.

Ps All money from this video will be donated to @momsdemand ❤️. 

#popculture #movies #film #moviereview #whattowatch"
content.text: Typically I would never ever purposefully spoil a movie the same weekend that it was released, but for “The Drama” it seems like a responsible thing to do ❤️.I genuinely think The Drama was VERY well done, it was a really good movie!! The performances were fantastic and the story actually handled a really intense conversation in a very impactful and often very nuanced way. But I just wish I had known that this is the type of movie I was in for. Have you seen it? Will you see it? Let me know below.Ps All money from this video will be donated to @momsdemand ❤️. #popculture #movies #film #moviereview #whattowatchI just got out of the movie and came to see what you had said about it. I went in completely blind and I'm glad that I did. Strangely I was not at all triggered by the school shooting part of it. The rest of my comment is going to be a little spoilery so if people don't want to read it, here is your warning. I was way more triggered by the graphic image of the 12-year-old dying in a car accident than anything else in the movie. Obviously you know I'm a teacher and literally have to take frequent trainings on what happens if a school shooter comes onto campus and I have to carry around an emergency button around my neck in case of an active shooter every day of my life, so it's constantly on my mind, but I personally think that Rachel locking up a mentally disabled boy and leaving him in the forest and not telling anybody, even when questioned... I think that was way worse than a depressed teenager fantasizing about hurting the people that were hurting her. Maybe that is an insane take. Maybe I just hear frequently about kids who are constantly exposed to school shootings that genuinely look at it as a viable option but then never follow through. I just think the fact that Emma (Zendaya) recognized that it was the worst part of her life, and ended up literally doing a 180 and becoming an activist against gun violence showed way more character growth than Rachel who laughed it off and said it wasn't a big deal and never fessed up.This is fascinating!! I feel like they marketed in such a way that I expected something huge, maybe triggering and shocking for sure. The trailer veryyyy much hints at that. I wasn’t “shocked” by there being something shocking at all. I actually expected something much, much worse from all the people saying it was super triggering.I thought the marketing was clear. I didn’t know WHAT the plot twist was exactly but from the trailer of them sharing their worst actions and the looks after it was her turn, I was thinking it had to be something terrible, like trying to ☠️ your sibling or something equally bad. I just didn’t realize she was the only person who didn’t actually go through with being a terrible person.I don’t think EVERYONE needs to know. There’s something about going in not knowing that makes it all the more impactful, which is why they didn’t advertise it like that. If you’re someone who’s going to get triggered by stuff, that’s what the rating system is for. Not even saying that’s a bad thing, but people should probably start looking at the reasons why movies are rated the way they are and then deciding what’s safe for them to see right away and what they should wait a little and look into before deciding to go to the theaters. But either way the actual trailer itself doesn’t seem super cutesy and happy, and it’s an A24. I expected a shock and that’s what it isI normally hate knowing this kind of thing before a movie, but I am SO glad I knew what the secret was going in. I don't think it ruined my experience at all. It meant I was able to actually process the movie instead of being freaked out the whole time that there would actually be a shooting on screen.The Autistics (me) in the audience knew what was gonna happen.This was a horrible film.Rob n zendaya. Romantic scenes got me like 🙈🙈It a dark comedy either way education concept it not for everyone !!I love also the romance part 🙈🙈🙈I heard a few times ppl thought it was a rom-com. They must have seen another trailer, I never thought of rom-comI don't think the trailer gave off rom com at ALL. It's very obvious it's going to be at times dark and something serious with how her friends and fiancée reacted. However, I do 100% agree on you giving this spoiler. It's not a topics that triggers me, but the imagery is very dark and I can see how it can trigger so many people. Especially the DJ scene.
